findings.title: Status includes a session beyond the exclusive end date
findings.description: The wanted-range check uses interval overlap. CME sessions open the evening before their session date, so for a wanted range ending at midnight on date D, the session dated D can still satisfy `session.open_utc < wanted[1]` and be included. This reports an out-of-range session and can affect the caught-up result. Scope wanted sessions by the intended session-date range, while retaining the separate held-session inclusion.

findings.title: Caught-up can be true when the open-ended range has no known edge
findings.description: When a tier and start are configured but no dataset edge or explicit end is available, `wanted_end` is `None`, so `_scope` can return no sessions if none are held. `caught_up` is nevertheless called with `wanted=True`; its `all(...)` over an empty sequence returns `True`. The status can therefore claim the product is caught up without knowing the range to check. Keep this result indeterminate until the range is bounded.

findings.title: Coverage repeatedly scans all range keys for every session
findings.description: For each session, `_session_row` constructs and iterates a tuple of every key in both range-wide totals dictionaries, then filters by date. This makes the work grow roughly with the number of sessions multiplied by the total number of instrument/session keys, with a full tuple allocation per session. Group totals by session date once, then look up only that session’s keys.

findings.title: No load test covers the new status and coverage read paths
findings.description: The added integration coverage exercises only two sessions and checks functional parity. The new commands make database/network reads, and `coverage` performs a raw `tick_trade` scan over a caller-selected range; there is no load-tier test bounding latency, throughput, or resource use for these paths. Add a realistic-range load test and gate it as required for network-path changes.
